newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Britain's Princess Diana meets Nelson Mandela.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Princess Diana meets Nelson Mandela.

text.p: Diana, Princess of Wales, met South African President Nelson Mandela on Monday and won his praise for having influenced his government to ban the making of anti-personnel mines.
Diana, in a brief appearance with Mandela on the steps of his official Cape Town residence, told reporters most of their 30-minute meeting had focused on South Africa's AIDS problem.
"I came here to discuss the situation of AIDS in the country with the president and that's what we've been discussing," she said. "I said if I can help in any way, I'm available to do it."
Diana, who was divorced from the British royal heir Prince Charles last year, said she had been "absolutely thrilled" to meet Mandela.
The South African president said he had complimented the princess on her efforts to help AIDS sufferers and on her campaign against landmines.
"I complimented her for visiting Angola and seeing the crippled children, crippled by landmines and so on...

"To some extent we were influenced by the lead which she took in this regard," said Mandela, whose country banned the production of anti-personnel mines last month and undertook to destroy its stockpiles of the weapons.
Diana arrived in Cape Town over the weekend to visit her brother, Earl Spencer, who lives in one of the city's affluent suburbs.
Since her divorce she has sought to create an international role for herself as an ambassador for good causes.

In January she paid a high profile visit to mine victims in Angola as part of a campaign by humanitarian groups for a global ban on the weapons, which have maimed or killed countless civilians around the world.
Mandela said he had "trembled" at meeting Diana. "I didn't know that I would meet a British princess."
Asked by photographers to give her a kiss, the president demurred, saying:
Mandela, twice divorced, last year made public his love affair with Graca Machel, the widow of Samora Machel who led Mozambique after independence from Portugal.
